case_studies.title: Experimental Performance of a 5G N78 Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface: From Controlled Measurements to Commercial Network Deployment
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a real-world experimental analysis of a modular reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) prototype designed to operate in the 5G N78 band. Unlike most RIS studies in the literature that focus on simulations or controlled setups, the proposed system is validated through three phases consisting of indoor measurements, outdoor long-range tests, and deployment in a live commercial 5G standalone network. The RIS is exploited to enhance coverage in a non-line-of-sight (NLoS) zone, identified through baseline drive tests. Results show promising gains in RSRP and SINR, while also r
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the enhancement of coverage in non-line-of-sight zones in 5G networks. The AI approach used is a modular reconfigurable intelligent surface prototype designed to operate in the 5G N78 band. The outcome of the study shows promising gains in RSRP and SINR, indicating the potential of the proposed system to improve network coverage.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can design and test reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in various environments to optimize their performance. By validating the system through multiple phases of testing, including indoor measurements, outdoor long-range tests, and deployment in live commercial networks, practitioners can ensure the reliability and effectiveness of their solution.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed system can be monetized by offering it as a product or service to telecommunications companies seeking to improve their network coverage. The company can also provide maintenance and update services to ensure the system remains effective and efficient in changing network conditions.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is hindered by the need for real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. The authors propose a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization, evaluating model-hardware pairs under Cost, Energy, and Time metrics. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient than desktop-grade GPUs, offering a potential solution for on-robot deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners should consider the importance of model-hardware co-characterization and evaluate their models on various edge accelerators to find the optimal balance between cost, energy, and time. By doing so, they can develop more efficient and scalable AI models for real-world applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The research presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing robot control systems, as the proposed approach can enable more efficient and cost-effective deployment of VLA models on robots. This can lead to the development of new products or services, such as autonomous robots for industrial or household tasks, with improved performance and reduced energy consumption.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, Computer Vision, NLP, MLOps

case_studies.title: PhyCo: Learning Controllable Physical Priors for Generative Motion
case_studies.abstract: Modern video diffusion models excel at appearance synthesis but still struggle with physical consistency: objects drift, collisions lack realistic rebound, and material responses seldom match their underlying properties. We present PhyCo, a framework that introduces continuous, interpretable, and physically grounded control into video generation. Our approach integrates three key components: (i) a large-scale dataset of over 100K photorealistic simulation videos where friction, restitution, deformation, and force are systematically varied across diverse scenarios; (ii) physics-supervised fine-
case_studies.summary: Modern video diffusion models often lack physical consistency, resulting in unrealistic object movements and interactions. The proposed PhyCo framework addresses this issue by introducing continuous, interpretable, and physically grounded control into video generation through a large-scale dataset and physics-supervised fine-tuning. This approach enables more realistic video generation with improved physical consistency, making it useful for various applications such as video editing, gaming, and simulation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize large-scale datasets of simulated videos with varying physical properties to fine-tune their models and improve physical consistency. By integrating physics-supervised learning into their models, practitioners can generate more realistic videos with enhanced object movements and interactions.
case_studies.monetisation: The PhyCo framework offers a clear product opportunity in the video editing and gaming industries, where realistic video generation is crucial for creating engaging user experiences. Companies can leverage this technology to develop more advanced video editing tools or game development software, providing a competitive edge in the market.

case_studies.title: DEFault++: Automated Fault Detection, Categorization, and Diagnosis for Transformer Architectures
case_studies.abstract: Transformer models are widely deployed in critical AI applications, yet faults in their attention mechanisms, projections, and other internal components often degrade behavior silently without raising runtime errors. Existing fault diagnosis techniques often target generic deep neural networks and cannot identify which transformer component is responsible for an observed symptom. In this article, we present DEFault++, a hierarchical learning-based diagnostic technique that operates at three level of abstraction: it detects whether a fault is present, classifies it into one of 12 transformer-sp
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the problem of silent faults in transformer models that can degrade their behavior without raising runtime errors. The authors propose DEFault++, a hierarchical learning-based diagnostic technique that operates at three levels of abstraction to detect, classify, and diagnose faults in transformer architectures. The outcome is a more reliable and efficient fault diagnosis technique for transformer models, which can improve the performance and safety of AI applications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by incorporating hierarchical learning-based diagnostic techniques into their AI model development and testing pipelines. By doing so, they can identify and address potential faults in their transformer models, leading to more reliable and efficient AI systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The DEFault++ technique has the potential to be developed into a product or service that can be sold to companies that heavily rely on transformer models, such as those in the NLP or computer vision spaces. This product or service could offer automated fault detection and diagnosis capabilities, providing a competitive advantage to companies that adopt it.

case_studies.title: Design Structure Matrix Modularization with Large Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Design Structure Matrix (DSM) modularization, the task of partitioning system elements into cohesive modules, is a fundamental combinatorial challenge in engineering design. Traditional methods treat modularization as a pure graph optimization, without access to the engineering context embedded in the system. Building on prior work on LLM-based combinatorial optimization for DSM sequencing, this paper extends the method to modularization across five cases and three backbone LLMs. Our method achieves near-reference quality within 30 iterations without requiring specialized optimization code. Co
case_studies.summary: The problem of Design Structure Matrix (DSM) modularization is a fundamental challenge in engineering design, where traditional methods treat modularization as a pure graph optimization without considering the engineering context. This paper proposes an AI approach using Large Language Models (LLMs) to extend modularization across five cases and three backbone LLMs. The outcome achieves near-reference quality within 30 iterations without requiring specialized optimization code.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this method by leveraging LLMs to optimize combinatorial challenges in their respective domains, potentially reducing the need for specialized optimization code. By exploring the use of LLMs in modularization, practitioners can improve the efficiency and effectiveness of their design processes.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed method has a clear product opportunity in the engineering design and optimization software market, where companies can integrate LLM-based modularization into their existing design tools. This can lead to improved design efficiency, reduced costs, and increased competitiveness for companies that adopt this technology.

case_studies.title: Robustness Evaluation of a Foundation Segmentation Model Under Simulated Domain Shifts in Abdominal CT: Implications for Health Digital Twin Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. We present a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM (ViT-B) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. A standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol was used to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty. Controlled perturbations simulatin
case_studies.summary: The study evaluates the robustness of a foundation segmentation model under simulated domain shifts in abdominal CT scans, specifically for spleen segmentation. The researchers used a systematic slice-level robustness audit of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) and found that its robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. The outcome of the study highlights the need for further research to improve the model's robustness and generalizability to real-world clinical applications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this study's findings, AI practitioners can use a standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty and evaluate the robustness of their models under simulated domain shifts. By doing so, they can identify potential limitations and improve the generalizability of their models to real-world clinical applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing more robust and generalizable medical imaging models that can be deployed in clinical settings, such as hospitals and medical research institutions. A potential business opportunity is to develop a product that provides robust and accurate spleen segmentation in abdominal CT scans, which can be used to improve diagnosis and treatment of spleen-related diseases.

case_studies.title: Network Impact of Post-Quantum Certificate Chain sizes on Time to First Byte in TLS Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is a rapidly growing deployment challenge as cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) continue to advance, leaving traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509 vulnerable to attack. However, PQC introduces significant deployment challenges in real-world networks, with handshake sizes increasing from 5x to over 20x compared to classical algorithms. In this work, we evaluate the time to first byte (TTFB) under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning existing internet infrastructure to quantum-safe certificate s
case_studies.summary: The problem of transitioning to post-quantum cryptography in real-world networks is hindered by significant deployment challenges, including increased handshake sizes. The authors employ an AI-focused approach to evaluate the time to first byte under CDN-focused TLS conditions, characterizing the latency cost of transitioning to quantum-safe certificates. The outcome provides insights into the network impact of post-quantum certificate chain sizes on time to first byte in TLS deployments.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the potential latency costs when deploying post-quantum cryptography in real-world networks, and optimizing their solutions accordingly. By evaluating the time to first byte under various conditions, practitioners can better understand the performance implications of post-quantum cryptography and make informed decisions about its deployment.
case_studies.monetisation: The study highlights a clear need for efficient and scalable post-quantum cryptography solutions, presenting a potential business opportunity for companies that can develop and deploy optimized quantum-safe certificates. By addressing the latency costs associated with post-quantum cryptography, companies can provide valuable solutions for organizations seeking to transition to quantum-safe infrastructure.

case_studies.title: 3D Reconstruction Techniques in the Manufacturing Domain: Applications, Research Opportunities and Use Cases
case_studies.abstract: This comprehensive review examines the evolution and the current state of the art in three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction techniques in manufacturing applications. The analysis covers both traditional approaches and emerging deep learning methods, showing a critical research gap in unified 3d reconstruction frameworks. Through systematic review of 106 recent publications, we classify reconstruction techniques into three primary categories: data acquisition, point cloud generation, post-processing and applications. Non-contact methods, particularly structured light scanning and stereo vision,
case_studies.summary: The problem of 3D reconstruction in manufacturing applications is addressed through a comprehensive review of traditional and emerging deep learning methods. The AI approach involves analyzing 106 recent publications and classifying reconstruction techniques into three primary categories. The outcome is the identification of a critical research gap in unified 3D reconstruction frameworks, highlighting opportunities for future research and development.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the limitations of current 3D reconstruction techniques and exploring the potential of deep learning methods to improve accuracy and efficiency. By analyzing the classification of reconstruction techniques, practitioners can identify areas for improvement and develop more effective solutions for manufacturing applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The study highlights a concrete business opportunity for companies to develop and market unified 3D reconstruction frameworks that can be applied across various manufacturing applications. By addressing the research gap identified in the study, companies can create products that improve the efficiency and accuracy of 3D reconstruction, leading to increased adoption and revenue growth.

case_studies.title: A Pattern Language for Resilient Visual Agents
case_studies.abstract: Integrating multimodal foundation models into enterprise ecosystems presents a fundamental software architecture challenge. Architects must balance competing quality attributes: the high latency and non-determinism of vision language action (VLA) models versus the strict determinism and real-time performance required by enterprise control loops. In this study, we propose an architectural pattern language for visual agents that separates fast, deterministic reflexes from slow, probabilistic supervision. It consists of four architectural design patterns: (1) Hybrid Affordance Integration, (2) Ad
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the challenge of integrating multimodal foundation models into enterprise ecosystems, which requires balancing competing quality attributes such as latency and determinism. The proposed solution is an architectural pattern language for visual agents that separates fast, deterministic reflexes from slow, probabilistic supervision. This approach consists of four architectural design patterns, including Hybrid Affordance Integration, to improve the performance and reliability of visual agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can separate the fast and slow components of their visual agents, using deterministic models for real-time control loops and probabilistic models for supervisory tasks. By doing so, they can achieve a better balance between competing quality attributes and improve the overall performance and reliability of their systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed architectural pattern language has a clear product opportunity in industries that rely on computer vision and automation, such as robotics, healthcare, and manufacturing. Companies can develop and market products that implement this pattern language, providing a competitive edge in terms of performance, reliability, and scalability.

case_studies.title: ITS-Mina: A Harris Hawks Optimization-Based All-MLP Framework with Iterative Refinement and External Attention for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
case_studies.abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting plays a pivotal role in numerous real-world applications, including financial analysis, energy management, and traffic planning. While Transformer-based architectures have gained popularity for this task, recent studies reveal that simpler MLP-based models can achieve competitive or superior performance with significantly reduced computational cost. In this paper, we propose ITS-Mina, a novel all-MLP framework for multivariate time series forecasting that integrates three key innovations: (1) an iterative refinement mechanism that progressively enhances tem
case_studies.summary: The problem of multivariate time series forecasting is a significant challenge in various real-world applications, including financial analysis and energy management. The proposed AI approach, ITS-Mina, integrates an iterative refinement mechanism and external attention into an all-MLP framework to improve forecasting performance. The outcome is a novel framework that can potentially achieve competitive or superior performance with reduced computational cost.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by exploring the use of simpler MLP-based models for multivariate time series forecasting, and incorporating iterative refinement mechanisms to enhance performance. By doing so, they can potentially develop more efficient and effective forecasting models for various applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed framework has a clear potential for monetisation, as it can be adapted for various industries and applications, such as financial analysis and energy management, where accurate forecasting is crucial. A company can develop a product based on this framework, offering forecasting services to clients and generating revenue through subscription-based models or consulting services.

case_studies.title: From LLM-Driven Trading Card Generation to Procedural Relatedness: A Pokémon Case Study
case_studies.abstract: Since the dawn of Trading Card Games, the genre has grown into a multi-billion-dollar industry engaging millions of analog and digital players worldwide. Popular TCGs rely on regular updates, balance adjustments, and rotating constraints to sustain engagement. Yet, as metagames stabilize, predictable strategies dominate and viable card options diminish, often resulting in repetitive and impaired player experiences. This paper investigates the use of Large Language Models and Image Diffusion Models for Procedural Content Generation of TCG cards, addressing these challenges by enabling a persona
case_studies.summary: The Trading Card Game industry faces challenges with repetitive and impaired player experiences due to predictable strategies and limited card options. This paper proposes the use of Large Language Models and Image Diffusion Models for Procedural Content Generation of TCG cards to address these challenges. The outcome is the potential creation of new and engaging card content, enhancing the overall player experience.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by leveraging LLMs and Image Diffusion Models to generate procedural content for various applications, including game development and digital media. By integrating these models, practitioners can create dynamic and engaging content, improving user experience and driving user engagement.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed approach offers a clear product opportunity, enabling the creation of new and unique TCG cards, which can be monetized through in-game purchases, card sales, or subscription-based models. This can lead to significant revenue streams for game developers and publishers, particularly in the multi-billion-dollar TCG industry.

case_studies.title: Computing Equilibrium beyond Unilateral Deviation
case_studies.abstract: Most familiar equilibrium concepts, such as Nash and correlated equilibrium, guarantee only that no single player can improve their utility by deviating unilaterally. They offer no guarantees against profitable coordinated deviations by coalitions. Although the literature proposes solution concepts that provide stability against multilateral deviations (\emph{e.g.}, strong Nash and coalition-proof equilibrium), these generally fail to exist. In this paper, we study an alternative solution concept that minimizes coalitional deviation incentives, rather than requiring them to vanish, and is ther
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this paper is the limitation of traditional equilibrium concepts, such as Nash and correlated equilibrium, which only guarantee stability against unilateral deviations. The AI approach proposed is an alternative solution concept that minimizes coalitional deviation incentives. The outcome of this approach is a more robust and stable equilibrium concept that can handle multilateral deviations.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this concept by incorporating coalitional deviation incentives into their equilibrium models, allowing for more realistic and stable outcomes. This can be achieved by using advanced optimization techniques and game-theoretic frameworks to minimize deviation incentives.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity is to develop a software platform that implements this alternative solution concept, allowing companies to analyze and optimize their strategic decision-making processes. This platform could be marketed to industries where game-theoretic models are commonly used, such as finance, economics, and political science.

case_studies.title: Splitting Argumentation Frameworks with Collective Attacks and Supports
case_studies.abstract: This work proposes novel splitting techniques for argumentation formalisms that incorporate supports between defeasible elements. We base our studies on bipolar set-based argumentation frameworks (BSAFs) which generalize argumentation frameworks with collective attacks (SETAFs), as well as bipolar argumentation frameworks (BAFs), by incorporating both collective attacks and supports. Notably, BSAFs establish a crucial link to structured argumentation as they naturally capture general (potentially non-flat) assumption-based argumentation. The increase in expressiveness calls for diverse forms o
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the lack of effective splitting techniques for argumentation formalisms that incorporate supports between defeasible elements. The AI approach proposed is based on bipolar set-based argumentation frameworks (BSAFs), which generalize existing argumentation frameworks by incorporating both collective attacks and supports. The outcome of this study is the development of novel splitting techniques for BSAFs, which can potentially lead to more efficient and effective argumentation-based decision-making systems.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the use of BSAFs in their own argumentation-based systems, particularly in domains where collective attacks and supports are relevant. By incorporating BSAFs into their systems, practitioners can potentially improve the efficiency and effectiveness of their decision-making processes.
case_studies.monetisation: The research presented in this study can be monetised by developing commercial argumentation-based decision-making systems that incorporate BSAFs, which can be sold to organisations in various domains such as law, medicine, and finance. Companies can also offer consulting services to help organisations implement BSAF-based systems, providing a potential revenue stream.

case_studies.title: RHyVE: Competence-Aware Verification and Phase-Aware Deployment for LLM-Generated Reward Hypotheses
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) make reward design in reinforcement learning substantially more scalable, but generated rewards are not automatically reliable training objectives. Existing work has focused primarily on generating, evolving, or selecting reward candidates, while paying less attention to when such candidates can be verified and deployed during policy optimization. We study this deployment-time problem by treating generated rewards as reward hypotheses whose utility depends on the competence of the current policy and the phase of training. We propose \textsc{RHyVE}, a competence-awa
case_studies.summary: The problem of unreliable training objectives in reinforcement learning is addressed by proposing a system that treats generated rewards as reward hypotheses. The AI approach, called RHyVE, considers the competence of the current policy and the phase of training to verify and deploy these reward hypotheses. The outcome is a more scalable and reliable reward design process for reinforcement learning.
case_studies.how_to_apply: Practitioners can apply this approach by incorporating competence-aware verification and phase-aware deployment into their reinforcement learning pipelines, allowing for more efficient and effective policy optimization. By considering the utility of generated rewards in different phases of training, practitioners can improve the overall performance of their reinforcement learning systems.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity is to develop a product that integrates RHyVE into a reinforcement learning platform, offering scalable and reliable reward design as a key feature. This product could be marketed to companies working on complex control tasks, such as robotics or autonomous vehicles, where reliable reward design is crucial for successful policy optimization.

case_studies.title: SpecVQA: A Benchmark for Spectral Understanding and Visual Question Answering in Scientific Images
case_studies.abstract: Spectra are a prevalent yet highly information-dense form of scientific imagery, presenting substantial challenges to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) due to their unstructured and domain-specific characteristics. Here we introduce SpecVQA, a professional scientific-image benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding, covering 7 representative spectrum types with expert-annotated question-answer pairs. The aim comprises two aspects: spectra scientific QA evaluation and corresponding underlying task evaluation. SpecVQA contains 620 figures and 3100 QA p
case_studies.summary: The SpecVQA benchmark is designed to evaluate the ability of multimodal large language models to understand and answer questions about scientific spectral images. The benchmark consists of 620 figures and 3100 question-answer pairs, covering 7 representative spectrum types. The introduction of SpecVQA aims to improve the performance of multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding and visual question answering tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the SpecVQA benchmark, AI practitioners can use it to evaluate and fine-tune their multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding and visual question answering tasks. By using SpecVQA, practitioners can identify areas for improvement and develop more effective models for real-world applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The SpecVQA benchmark can be monetized by developing and selling multimodal models that have been fine-tuned on the benchmark, or by offering annotation and evaluation services for scientific spectral images. Companies can also use SpecVQA to develop and market AI-powered tools for scientific image analysis and question answering.

case_studies.title: Exploring Interaction Paradigms for LLM Agents in Scientific Visualization
case_studies.abstract: This paper examines how different types of large language model (LLM) agents perform on scientific visualization (SciVis) tasks, where users generate visualization workflows from natural-language instructions. We compare three primary interaction paradigms, including domain-specific agents with structured tool use, computer-use agents, and general-purpose coding agents, by evaluating eight representative agents across 15 benchmark tasks and measuring visualization quality, efficiency, robustness, and computational cost. We further analyze interaction modalities, including code scripts and mode
case_studies.summary: This study explores the effectiveness of large language model (LLM) agents in scientific visualization tasks, where users generate visualization workflows from natural-language instructions. The authors compared three interaction paradigms and evaluated eight representative agents across 15 benchmark tasks, measuring visualization quality, efficiency, robustness, and computational cost. The outcome of this study provides insights into the strengths and weaknesses of different LLM agents in scientific visualization tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by considering the trade-offs between different interaction paradigms and agent types when designing LLM-based systems for scientific visualization. By evaluating the performance of LLM agents on benchmark tasks, practitioners can identify the most suitable agents for their specific use cases and optimize their systems for better visualization quality and efficiency.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing and marketing specialized LLM-based tools for scientific visualization, which can be sold to research institutions, universities, or industries that rely heavily on data visualization. Companies can also offer customized LLM-based solutions for scientific visualization, providing clients with tailored agents and workflows that meet their specific needs and improve their visualization workflows.

case_studies.title: Graph World Models: Concepts, Taxonomy, and Future Directions
case_studies.abstract: As one of the mainstream models of artificial intelligence, world models allow agents to learn the representation of the environment for efficient prediction and planning. However, classical world models based on flat tensors face several key problems, including noise sensitivity, error accumulation and weak reasoning. To address these limitations, many recent studies use graph structure to decompose the environment into entity nodes and interactive edges, and model virtual environments in a structured space. This paper systematically formalizes and unifies these emerging graph-based works und
case_studies.summary: Classical world models in artificial intelligence face limitations such as noise sensitivity and weak reasoning. To address these issues, researchers are using graph structures to decompose environments into entity nodes and interactive edges. This approach allows for more efficient prediction and planning in virtual environments, but its applications and outcomes are still largely theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this concept by exploring graph-based models for their own environment representation and planning tasks, potentially leading to more robust and efficient solutions. By integrating graph structures into their existing models, practitioners can improve the reasoning and prediction capabilities of their AI agents.
case_studies.monetisation: The graph world model approach has potential for monetization in areas such as game development, simulation, and robotics, where more accurate and efficient environment representation can lead to improved user experience and automation. Companies can leverage this technology to create more realistic and interactive virtual environments, leading to new business opportunities in the fields of entertainment, education, and training.

case_studies.title: Feasible-First Exploration for Constrained ML Deployment Optimization in Crash-Prone Hierarchical Search Spaces
case_studies.abstract: Deploying machine learning models under production constraints requires joint optimization over model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This induces a hierarchical mixed-variable search space in which many configurations are invalid: evaluations may crash, exceed memory limits, or violate latency constraints. Standard black-box optimizers such as Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE) and constrained Bayesian optimization are effective when valid configurations are common, but they can spend a large fraction of a small evaluation budget on invalid or uni
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying machine learning models under production constraints is addressed in this study, which proposes a feasible-first exploration approach to optimize model deployment. This approach aims to navigate the hierarchical mixed-variable search space and avoid invalid configurations that can lead to crashes or exceeded memory limits. The outcome of this approach is a more efficient optimization process that can handle constrained machine learning deployment, but its practical implementation and impact are still theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can prioritize the exploration of feasible configurations in their optimization process, using techniques such as constrained Bayesian optimization to efficiently search the hierarchical search space. By doing so, they can reduce the waste of evaluation budget on invalid configurations and improve the overall efficiency of their model deployment optimization.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed approach can be monetized by developing a product or service that offers optimized machine learning model deployment for businesses, which can lead to improved efficiency and reduced costs. This product or service can be integrated into existing MLOps pipelines, providing a clear value proposition for companies looking to streamline their machine learning operations.
